chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a junub who has sores on him. He said: “There is no harm in his not performing ghusl; he performs tayammum.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ritual purification
key_terms.الْقُرُوحُ: sores or wounds on the body
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or objection
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: to perform tayammum, dry ablution as a substitute purification
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلَ: to perform ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a junub with sores who cannot perform ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person in a state of janabah who has sores or wounds that make ghusl harmful or difficult. Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام states that in such a case, there is no harm in leaving ghusl and performing tayammum instead.
